_comment: Per-provider speech capabilities. Sibling of llm_defaults.json and read the same way: services/speech/config.py loads this once at import and every capability lookup goes through it, so shared code never branches on a provider name. Values here were verified against live official docs; see docs-internal/speech_provider_rfc.md section 7 for the sources and for the handful of items the docs do not state. Per-model overrides use the same {'model-id': value, '_default': value} shape as llm_defaults.json's max_output_tokens.
_common_languages_comment: Fallback for the Language dropdown when a provider does not declare a closed list of its own. OpenAI/Whisper, Deepgram and Groq accept far more codes than these; this is a convenience shortlist, and 'Auto-detect' (empty value) is always offered first. A provider WITH a closed set (Sarvam) declares `languages` in its own block and that wins.

tts._voices_comment: 13 voices exist, but tts-1 and tts-1-hd support only the first 9. Per-model override rather than a flat list so the node can validate before the provider 400s.
tts._instructions_comment: Steerability via the `instructions` body field is gpt-4o-mini-tts only; it is silently ignored on tts-1 / tts-1-hd.

stt._response_formats_comment: Model-gated, and getting this wrong is a 400 rather than a degraded result. Because timestamp_granularities requires verbose_json, word timestamps are effectively whisper-1 only.

groq._comment: Serves OpenAI's exact transcription wire format at its own base URL, so it rides the same provider class. Transcription-only: no TTS product.

stt._translate_comment: The turbo model omits translation entirely; only whisper-large-v3 can translate.
stt._min_billed_comment: Groq bills a 10-second floor regardless of clip length; the provider reports max(duration, 10).

tts._endpoint_comment: voice_id is a PATH segment, and output_format is a QUERY parameter rather than a body field. Sending output_format in the JSON body yields the default silently instead of an error.
tts._tier_gated_comment: mp3 at 192 kbps needs Creator+; PCM and WAV at 44.1 kHz need Pro+. A tier miss surfaces as a permission error, which is why the panel does not pre-filter.
tts._speed_comment: The OpenAPI schema allows 0.5-2.0 while the best-practices guide recommends 0.7-1.2. Both are official and were never reconciled, so the API bound is enforced and the narrower range is guidance only.

deepgram._comment: Options are QUERY parameters, audio is sent as a RAW body with an audio/* Content-Type (not multipart), and auth is 'Authorization: Token <key>' rather than Bearer. All three differ from every other provider here.

stt._default_model_comment: Deepgram's own documented default is base-general, which is not what anyone wants in 2026, so an explicit default is set here rather than inherited.
stt._smart_format_comment: smart_format supersedes punctuate and additionally applies paragraphing plus number/date/currency formatting.
stt._max_upload_comment: VERIFIED from the Limits section of the pre-recorded-audio docs: 2 GB maximum file size. That is far above services.media's own 25 MiB read cap, which is therefore the binding limit in practice — the value is recorded for accuracy, not because it will ever be hit here. (An earlier revision claimed no cap was published; that was wrong.)
stt._max_duration_comment: ALSO verified, and this one bites: a synchronous request over 10 minutes of audio (Nova/Base/Enhanced) or 20 minutes (Whisper) returns 504 Gateway Timeout rather than a transcript. Long recordings need Deepgram's callback flow, which this node does not implement.

sarvam._comment: Indic-first. TTS returns base64 inside a JSON array rather than raw bytes, and long input comes back as several standalone clips that must not be byte-concatenated.

tts._sample_rate_comment: Sarvam's own docs disagree with themselves here: the OpenAPI schema says 22050 while the field description says 24000. 24000 matches what the previous node shipped and what the description states.

stt._timestamps_comment: Timestamps and diarization exist only on the batch job API, never on this synchronous endpoint. The response fields are always null here.
